It did not ask the tenant to give a spare key to the agency or landlord. It also did not tell the landlord that the record shows no lock change; that point appears only in an internal note. items.reasoning: The agent made no reference to the tenancy agreement's alterations or pets clauses, or to the dog mentioned in events 006/007. The tone with the tenant was courteous, but the linking part of this item is missing.
The agent treated the lock change as a routine question and set a follow-up three days out. It did not frame the missing key as an access or safety issue needing prompt resolution.
The agent did not tell the landlord the inspection was closed with no issues, and it took follow-up action.
The tenant was asked questions. They were not told to remove the flap or hand over keys immediately.
The case was not closed, and a follow-up was recorded.
The landlord's email was acted on, with recorded actions for both items.

grades.overall_note: The agent handled the landlord's new issues sensibly: it contacted the tenant, acknowledged the landlord and set a follow-up. It fell short on the key, though. It did not ask for a spare key to be provided or tell the landlord that the record shows no lock change. It also never flagged that the covering email said 'no issues' while the report noted the dog flap.
